holidays.name: National Ballpoint Pen Day
holidays.description: A salute to the humble pen that has been smudging your sleeves and signing your contracts for decades. Click one, scribble a note, and enjoy the satisfying glide of ink on paper.
holidays.origin: The day honors the ballpoint pen. Hungarian journalist László Bíró patented the modern version in the 1930s, and the day itself is an unofficial observance. Bíró noticed that the ink used in newspaper printing dried quickly and left paper smudge-free. He then designed a pen that used a tiny rolling ball to deliver thick, quick-drying ink.
holidays.funFact: In Argentina and several other countries, ballpoint pens are still called 'birome', after Bíró and his business partner Juan Jorge Meyne, who went by Biro-Meyne.

holidays.name: National Iced Tea Day
holidays.description: A day to pour something cold over ice and toast the summer's most refreshing beverage. Sweet, unsweet, lemony or peachy, every glass counts.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food and drink observance of unclear origin. It lands in early summer, when cold drinks are most welcome.
holidays.funFact: Iced tea is often said to have become a national sensation at the 1904 St. Louis World's Fair, where a heat wave drove fairgoers away from hot tea and toward cold glasses.

holidays.name: National Herbs and Spices Day
holidays.description: A fragrant day for anyone who believes dinner needs more oregano. Open the spice rack, try something new, and rescue that jar of paprika you bought three years ago.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial culinary observance of unclear origin. It encourages home cooks to explore the flavors that make food interesting.
holidays.funFact: Spices were once so valuable that pepper was sometimes called 'black gold' and was used in medieval Europe to pay rent and dowries.
